blockers.title: The IKCONFIG derivation accepts an arbitrary or partial marker blob as structural proof
evidence: kexecAbsenceDerivation first searches the entire PE member byte string for IKCFG_ST and IKCFG_ED. It does not require exactly one ordered pair, define which pair wins, restrict the pair to the loaded/decompressed kernel payload, or reject pairs in a non-executed PE section, overlay, certificate table, embedded payload, or other data region.

If any raw pair is found, the specified search order does not decompress and inspect the actual kernel payload. A compressed kexec-enabled kernel can therefore carry a raw decoy pair outside its payload while its genuine IKCONFIG with CONFIG_KEXEC=y remains hidden in the compressed payload.

The extract rule calls any successfully gunzipped bytes between the markers 'kernel .config text' without requiring CONFIG_IKCONFIG=y, a complete canonical Kconfig serialization, a version/schema bind, unique symbol assignments, or even a non-partial configuration. The requiredN rule then treats every missing symbol as equivalent to n. An empty or selective decoy config consequently yields kexec-absent.

Concrete counterexample: authenticated K has CONFIG_KEXEC=y and CONFIG_SYSCTL=n in its genuine compressed payload, so kexec works while /proc/sys/kernel/kexec_load_disabled is absent. K's exact PE member also contains a raw non-loaded IKCFG_ST + gzip(partial config with the five required names omitted) + IKCFG_ED region. v36 takes the raw branch, derives kexec-absent, the signed PATHLESS field echoes that result, procfs corroboration is absent, and NT-TCB-KEXEC passes. K can then enter undeclared M.

The restored path/hash/PE joins authenticate the bytes containing both the executable kernel and the decoy; they do not establish that the selected marker blob governed compilation. Signed carriage authenticates the flawed derivation result for this entry but does not independently validate which config produced the executable code.

Because one permitted parse can issue a positive fail-closed capability for a kexec-capable exact member, this is not merely an over-refusal or test-vector omission. It preserves the post-boot replacement false allow that the new capability is intended to close.
blockers.impact: A kexec-enabled, exactly authenticated kernel can be signed and qualified as kexec-absent, then replace itself with an undeclared kernel. The live OS-ABI TCB remains open despite the new signed capability field.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define an architecture-pinned canonical kernel-payload parser and accept exactly one official IKCONFIG pair inside that selected loaded/decompressed payload; reject zero, duplicate, nested, out-of-region, or ambiguous pairs. Validate a complete canonical Kconfig serialization and require each proof symbol to have an explicit version-appropriate disabled value rather than treating arbitrary omission as n. Bind the configuration to signed build provenance for the exact member, or use another independently verifiable capability proof that cannot be satisfied by inert member bytes. Signed carriage should attest that validated result, not substitute for validation.

shouldFix.title: The compressed-kernel fallback is x86-specific, format-incomplete, and under-specified
evidence: The slice-1 Linux set includes both linux/x86_64 and linux/arm64, but the fallback has no architecture dispatch and only says to read an x86 bzImage setup_header payload_offset and payload_length.

An arm64 EFI zboot image does not use the x86 setup_header layout. When its genuine IKCONFIG is inside the compressed payload rather than visible in the outer PE wrapper, v36 has no defined way to locate it and refuses an otherwise in-scope direct EFI-stub boot.

Even for x86, the contract does not define the setup_header byte offsets, endianness, header magic/version checks, the base to which payload_offset is relative, overlap/bounds rules, or decompression output limits. Independent implementations can select different payload bytes.

The compression enum lists gzip, xz, zstd, and lz4 but omits other Linux kernel compression formats such as bzip2, lzma, and lzo. Those images fail derivation even though inScopeBootConfigs does not exclude them and refusesBootConfigs describes only missing IKCONFIG, not an unsupported otherwise-valid kernel-image format.
These gaps primarily over-refuse valid machines rather than create the decoy false allow in PTCB-V36-B1, so they are recorded separately as determinacy and scope defects.
shouldFix.impact: Conforming reviewers can disagree on x86 payload extraction, and valid slice-1 arm64 or differently compressed x86 EFI-stub kernels can become unqualifiable without a declared platform/configuration exclusion.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Dispatch on the complete platformProfile architecture and pin exact x86 bzImage and arm64 Image/EFI-zboot layouts, including offsets, byte order, magic/version, bounds, and resource limits. Support the complete declared compression set or explicitly narrow inScopeBootConfigs and refusal text to a justified closed subset. Add positive, malformed, and cross-architecture vectors.

verdictBasis: REJECT because ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX; this review finds 1 blocker and 1 SHOULD-FIX finding.
conclusion: REJECT. v36 reproduces its custody pins, restores the exact authenticated kernel-member joins, signs the capability on the same PATHLESS entry, demotes procfs to corroboration, and restores the FilePathList parser. Its new structural proof is still unsafe: an unrestricted, non-unique raw IKCONFIG marker search plus absence-means-n accepts a partial or decoy config while a kexec-enabled real payload remains compressed. The fallback is also x86-specific and incomplete for the declared Linux image set. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains in D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
